unit.title: Plants are living things
unit.blurb: Alive or not alive, the parts of a plant, and what plants need to grow.

O1.t: Sort things into living, once living and never alive, and know that plants are living things.

O2.t: Name the roots, stem, leaves and flowers of a plant and say what each part does.

O3.t: Know that plants need light to grow well, and grow towards the light.

O4.t: Know that plants need water and the right temperature to stay healthy.

captions: Hello, little scientists!
Some things are alive. Some things are not. Let's find out how to tell!
This is lesson 1.1: alive or not alive?
Look at this puppy.
The puppy eats, drinks and grows bigger.
Now look at this teddy.
The teddy never eats. It never grows.
The puppy is alive. The teddy is not alive.
Living things can do special things.
They need food and water.
They grow.
And they move. Even plants move a little, towards the light!
Pause and think.
Which one is alive?
Is a plant alive?
Yes! A plant starts as a tiny seedling.
It drinks water, and it grows bigger and bigger.
Then it makes flowers and seeds. Plants are living things!
Some things were never alive.
A rock was never alive.
A car and a spoon were never alive.
They do not eat, drink or grow.
Did you know?
Some trees are very, very old.
They have been alive for thousands of years!
Riddle time!
I grow every year, but I am not alive. What am I?
Your age! It grows on every birthday!
Your turn.
Is a rock alive?
Let's go on an alive hunt!
Go into a garden or a park, with an adult.
Find some living things, like plants and ants.
Find some things that are not alive, like stones. Sort them into two groups!
Let's remember.
Living things need food and water, and they grow.
Plants are living things.
Animals are living things too.
A rock was never alive. Super work, little scientists!

captions: Hello, little scientists!
Plants have different parts. Let's meet them!
This is lesson 1.2: parts of a plant.
A plant has four main parts.
The roots are under the ground.
The stem holds the plant up.
The leaves are green. And the flower is often bright and pretty!
Let's look at the roots.
Roots grow down into the soil.
They drink up water for the plant, like a straw.
And they hold the plant in the ground, so the wind cannot blow it away.
Pause and think.
Which part of a plant takes in water?
The stem is like a road.
It carries water up to the leaves.
The leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.
And the flowers make seeds, so new plants can grow.
We eat lots of plant parts!
A carrot is a root.
Lettuce is made of leaves.
Broccoli is little flowers. Yummy!
Did you know?
A tree trunk is a stem too. A giant, woody stem!
Joke time!
Why did the gardener plant a light bulb?
Because she wanted to grow a power plant!
Your turn.
Which part of a plant makes seeds?
Let's see the stem carry water!
Put water in a jar, and add some food colour.
Stand a stick of celery in the jar.
Wait one day. The colour climbs up the stem to the leaves!
Let's remember.
Roots take in water, and hold the plant in the ground.
The stem holds the plant up, and carries water.
Leaves make food.
And flowers make seeds. Blooming brilliant!

captions: Hello, little scientists!
Do plants need light? Let's find out!
This is lesson 1.3: plants need light.
We have two bean plants.
We put one plant by a sunny window.
We put the other plant in a dark cupboard.
Then we wait for two weeks.
Look what happened!
The plant by the window is green and strong.
The plant in the cupboard is pale, yellow and weak.
So plants need light to grow well.
Pause and think.
Which plant grew best?
Why do plants need light?
Leaves catch the sunlight.
They use the light to make food for the plant.
No light means no food!
Put a plant on a windowsill.
After a few days, it bends towards the window.
Plants grow towards the light.
Young sunflowers even turn to follow the Sun!
Did you know?
Astronauts grow lettuce in space!
They use special lamps to give the plants light.
Joke time!
What did the big flower say to the little flower?
Hi, bud!
Your turn.
What happens to a plant kept in the dark?
Let's do a light test.
Get two small plants. Give them the same water.
Put one by a window. Cover the other one with a big box.
Look after one week. Which plant is greener?
Let's remember.
Plants need light to grow well.
Leaves use light to make food.
Plants kept in the dark go pale and weak.
And plants grow towards the light. Sunny work!

captions: Hello, little scientists!
What else do plants need? Let's find out!
This is lesson 1.4: plants need water and the right temperature.
Here is a happy plant.
Oh no! Nobody gave it water for a whole week.
The leaves droop down. We say the plant wilts.
Plants need water to stay alive.
Let's give it a drink of water.
Wait a few hours.
Hooray! The plant stands up tall again!
But be careful. Too much water can hurt a plant too.
Pause and think.
What does a plant do when it has no water?
Plants also need the right temperature.
If it is too cold, a plant can freeze.
If it is too hot, a plant can dry up.
Most plants like it warm. Not too hot and not too cold.
So what do plants need?
They need light.
They need water.
And they need warmth. Most plants also grow in soil.
Did you know?
A cactus can live in the hot, dry desert.
It stores water inside its fat stem!
Joke time!
What do you call a tree that is always sad?
A weeping willow!
Your turn.
Where would a plant grow best?
Let's do a water test.
Get two small plants, and put them in the same sunny place.
Water one plant every day. Do not water the other one.
Look after one week. What happened?
Let's remember.
Plants need water. Without water, they wilt.
Plants need the right temperature: not too hot, not too cold.
So plants need light, water and warmth.
Green-fingered work, little scientists!
